questionText:
Consider the entries shown below in the forwarding table of an IP router. Each entry consists of an IP prefix and the corresponding next hop router for packets whose destination IP address matches the prefix. The notation "/N" in a prefix indicates a subnet mask with the most significant N bits set to 1.

PrefixNext hop router
10.1.1.0/24R1
10.1.1.128/25R2
10.1.1.64/26R3
10.1.1.192/26R4

This router forwards 20 packets each to 5 hosts. The IP addresses of the hosts are 10.1.1.16, 10.1.1.72, 10.1.1.132, 10.1.1.191, and 10.1.1.205 . The number of packets forwarded via the next hop router R2 is ________
explanation:
To determine the number of packets forwarded via next hop router R2, we find the routing path for each destination IP address using the Longest Prefix Match rule.

Prefix Ranges & Mask Lengths:
• $10.1.1.0/24$: $10.1.1.0$ to $10.1.1.255$ (Mask length = 24)
• $10.1.1.128/25$: $10.1.1.128$ to $10.1.1.255$ (Mask length = 25)
• $10.1.1.64/26$: $10.1.1.64$ to $10.1.1.127$ (Mask length = 26)
• $10.1.1.192/26$: $10.1.1.192$ to $10.1.1.255$ (Mask length = 26)

Next Hop Determination for Hosts:
1. 10.1.1.16: Matches $10.1.1.0/24$. Next hop = R1
2. 10.1.1.72: Matches $10.1.1.0/24$ and $10.1.1.64/26$. Longest match is $/26$. Next hop = R3
3. 10.1.1.132: Matches $10.1.1.0/24$ and $10.1.1.128/25$. Longest match is $/25$. Next hop = R2
4. 10.1.1.191: Matches $10.1.1.0/24$ and $10.1.1.128/25$ (Note: $10.1.1.192/26$ starts at .192). Longest match is $/25$. Next hop = R2
5. 10.1.1.205: Matches $10.1.1.0/24$, $10.1.1.128/25$, and $10.1.1.192/26$. Longest match is $/26$. Next hop = R4

Total Packets to R2:
Hosts forwarded to R2 are $10.1.1.132$ and $10.1.1.191$ ($2$ hosts).
Since $20$ packets are sent to each host, the total number of packets forwarded via R2 = $2 \times 20 = 40$.
